newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak army commander supports NATO membership.
newsitem.headline: Slovak army commander supports NATO membership.

text.p: Slovakia's army could suffer if the country fails to win membership of NATO in the first wave, the chief of the Slovak general staff said on Tuesday.

"We have done so much to prepare for integration in NATO, that our exclusion from the first wave of applicants could have several negative effects on the army," General Jozef Tuchyna said in an interview with the independent daily Pravda.

"Professional soldiers will ask whether it was worth devoting so much effort, and people could start ask whether the money spent for NATO partnership projects could not have been better spent," Tuchyna said.

Slovak interest in cooperation with NATO would not abate even if the country was not in the first wave of new members, he said, but added that such a development would "surely postpone possible future integration into the alliance."
Slovakia will have to continue to cooperate with the Russian army for longer due to the fact that the Slovak army uses mainly Russian materiel, he said.
"But I can responsibly state that there is no military pressure from Russia to join them in their negative attitude towards NATO enlargement," Tuchyna said.

Slovakia is keen to be among the first new members of NATO, but its chances are believed to have waned after Western criticism of the pace of democratic reform. The country will hold a referendum on NATO membership on May 23 and 24.
NATO is scheduled to invite prospective new members to start membership negotiations at its summit in Madrid in July.
The Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovenia are the most often mentioned countries to form the first wave of states invited for the membersip talks in the summer.
The cabinet of Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar has stated membership in the EU and NATO as top foreign policy priorities.
